intended_object: The norm map N_{G/S} : (A^S)_{G/S} → A^G, taken for every open normal subgroup S of the profinite group G and assembled into a natural transformation. Its source is the inverse system of finite coinvariants, whose transition maps for S ≤ T are the residual norms N_{T/S}. Its target is the constant system A^G. This is the middle map of the finite Tate norm sequence 0 → Ĥ^{-1} → (A^S)_{G/S} → A^G → Ĥ^0 → 0. I took this from the docstring, the module documentation and the `_app` simp lemma.
explanation:
At each level S the component is `normFromFiniteCoinvariants A L S`. That map is the continuous relative norm A^S → A^G, x ↦ Σ_{g ∈ G/S} g·x, passed to the coinvariants (A^S)_{G/S}. This is allowed because the norm is invariant under the action of G/S, which the library proves. Both sides carry the compact Hausdorff group topologies supplied by the `LevelCompact` structure.

The transition maps of the source diagram, `finiteCoinvariantDeflation`, are the residual norms N_{T/S} : (A^S)_{G/S} → (A^T)_{G/T}. The target diagram is constant at A^G with identity transitions. The naturality square is therefore the transitivity of norms, N_{G/T} ∘ N_{T/S} = N_{G/S}, which is exactly what the cited lemma proves.

This is the standard norm map of the Tate sequence, viewed as a morphism of inverse systems indexed by the open normal subgroups. There is nothing wrong in degenerate cases: for S = G the component is the identity of A^G, since the sum has one term. Mathlib has no continuous or profinite Tate cohomology, so there is no counterpart there. The setting (a profinite group G, a representation A, a level-compact structure L) is the library's own framework for this construction and is what the construction needs, so the definition is not too narrow.
